- Overestimate prices in bullish sentiment periods (positive sentiment > 0.0) — model tends to overshoot, especially after recent spikes.
- Underestimate prices in bearish sentiment (negative sentiment < -0.3) — model fails to capture sharp downward momentum.
- Lagged corrections: if sentiment turns negative after a peak, model often holds high values for 2–3 days before dropping — adjust downward by 1–2% per day of lag.
- Mean reversion bias: model overreacts to short-term volatility; true price tends to revert to 10–15-day moving average after 3–5 days of extreme swings.
- Overshoot after spikes: if model forecasts a spike (e.g., >85) following a positive sentiment surge, reduce forecast by 5–10% for next 3–5 days to avoid overcorrection.
- Horizon-specific: 30-day forecasts are overly optimistic in early cycles — reduce by 2–5% if sentiment is neutral or mildly bearish.
- Sentiment-weighted adjustment: if sentiment > 0.1, reduce forecast by 1–3% for each day of positive sentiment; if sentiment < -0.2, increase forecast by 1–3% for each day of negative sentiment.
